question: Using Figure 2A-1 and Section 2A.11, describe the requirements for a retroreflective strip used on a sign support to enhance conspicuity.
model_answer: Direct Answer: The use of a retroreflective strip on a sign support is a permitted conspicuity-enhancement method, but once used it must meet strict requirements: the strip must be at least 2 inches wide, run the full length of the support from the sign down to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, match the sign's background color (with red required for YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs), and carry no legend or other information. A related mandatory application exists at passive grade crossings, where a white retroreflective strip is required on the back of Crossbuck supports. Standards (mandatory): - "If a strip of retroreflective material is used on the sign support, it shall be at least 2 inches in width, it shall be placed for the full length of the support from the sign to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, and its color shall match the background color of the sign, except that the color of the strip for the YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs shall be red. The retroreflective strip shall not display any legend or other information." - At passive grade crossings: "A vertical strip of retroreflective white material, not less than 2 inches in width, shall be used on each Crossbuck support at passive grade crossings for the full length of the back of the support from the Crossbuck sign or Number of Tracks plaque to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway... A white retroreflective strip wrapped around a round support... shall satisfy this requirement as long as the round support has an outside diameter of at least 2 inches." Options (permitted): - Based upon engineering judgment, where improved conspicuity of a standard regulatory, warning, or guide sign is desired, any of the methods illustrated in Figure 2A-1 may be used, including adding a strip of retroreflective material to the sign support. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-1, Example E, illustrates a vertical retroreflective strip (matching the fluorescent yellow-green background of a pedestrian warning sign) running down the support and terminating with a "2 ft MAX." dimension above the near edge of the roadway. [Image 3] Figure 8B-2 shows the grade-crossing application, depicting an optional 2-inch red or white retroreflective strip on the front of the Crossbuck support and the required 2-inch white retroreflective strip on the back of the support, extending to within 2 feet of the roadway edge. Citations: - Section 2A.11 Standard §5 (p.49) - Section 2A.11 Option §1 (p.49) - Section 8B.04 Standard §17 (p.1000) - Section 2A.21 Support §8 (p.62) - Figure 2A-1 (p.48) - Figure 8B-2 (p.997)
gold_answer: The strip must be at least 2 inches wide, extend from the sign down the full support to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, match the sign background color except that YIELD and DO NOT ENTER strips are red, and contain no legend or other information.
